gfi_title: Protein sequence, structure, and functionality database
vietnam_angle: Weak for building the database; moderate for contributing data. Local crops and side streams (mung bean, broken rice, rice bran, peanut, sesame, okara) have few published functionality data
vietnam_evidence: OpenAlex finds only a handful of Vietnam-affiliated papers on extraction or functionality of these crops since 2015, mostly lab-scale and focused on bioactive hydrolysates (SLP-01; SLP-02; SLP-07). One search found no open functionality database launched since 2021; the nearest public good is Embrapa's standard method set (SLP-10)
verdict_note: A sequence, structure and machine-learning database is a global research good Vietnam would use, not build. Vietnam's useful contribution is standardised functional data on its own crops, which belongs in the P4 extension proposed under GFI-017
signal_to_watch: An open functionality database (academic, GFI or Embrapa-led) that accepts Southeast Asian crop data; GFI APAC work on mung bean or rice proteins with open data

gfi_title: Plant-based ingredient analytical and characterization service
vietnam_angle: Real. Buyers already specify function (gel strength, emulsion and retort stability for meat pastes; solubility, viscosity and UHT stability for plant milks), and no Vietnamese laboratory offers functional testing as a service
vietnam_evidence: No entry in pilot_labs.csv lists functional or texture testing; one search found a dealer selling texture analysers but no fee-for-service offer (SLP-17). Buyer specifications are revealed in ch16 (BUY-05; BUY-16). Labs that could host: HUST protein characterisation group (PL-027), FIRI NACEFA (PL-002), Can Tho University Institute of Food and Biotechnology and Nguyen Tat Thanh University's hi-tech centre at Saigon Hi-Tech Park (SLP-01)
verdict_note: Extend P4 from protein quality to protein function: a standard functional panel (solubility, water and oil holding, emulsifying, foaming, gelling, per Embrapa 2022) plus buyer tests (gel strength in a sausage model, UHT stability), and an open dataset for local crops and side streams linked to the P5 atlas. Same owners and buyers as P4, so an extension, not a new public good
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese laboratory adding functional properties to its accredited scope; a buyer (Vinamilk, Vissan) publishing an ingredient specification
source_ids: GSD-01; SLP-01; SLP-10; SLP-17; BUY-05; BUY-16

gfi_title: Biological processing methods for isolating protein ingredients
scope_note: Processing of plant protein for food
vietnam_angle: Mixed. Enzyme-assisted extraction from broken rice has been done in Vietnam at lab scale, and broken rice now costs less per tonne than cassava starch. But rice protein pays only as a co-product of a starch or syrup line, and we found no such host in Vietnam. The mung bean starch-water route exists in China and Thailand, not at scale in Vietnam
vietnam_evidence: Viscozyme extraction of VD20 broken rice gave about 77% protein and about 55% recovery after 36 h (SLP-01). At USD 327 to 372 per t (FS-26) and 7.9 g protein per 100 g (DIE-12), raw material alone costs USD 5.1 to 6.6 per kg of product, against USD 2 to 3 for Chinese pea protein (our calculation; TPP-05). Rice protein is a by-product of rice syrup (SLP-08). Three searches found no Vietnamese rice starch, rice syrup or rice protein maker. Broken rice USD 368 to 372 per t (FS-26) against cassava native starch USD 520 to 540 per t FOB in April 2026 (FS-11)
verdict_note: Adds a constraint to T10 (rice arm): a rice protein ingredient needs a host that sells the carbohydrate, so the rice arm is a co-product of a broken-rice saccharification line, not a stand-alone isolate plant. Adds a note to T4: broken rice is a second, protein-bearing sugar feedstock while cassava starch prices stay high. Enzymes are a tool inside T10, not a separate play
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese starch, syrup or beer-adjunct processor announcing broken-rice saccharification; Chinese or Thai rice-protein offers to Vietnamese dairy buyers; cassava starch falling back below about USD 420 per t

gfi_title: Fiber spinning innovations for improved plant protein texturization
scope_note: Texturisation of plant protein for food
vietnam_angle: None now. Vietnam has no documented texturisation capacity beyond machine dealers; the frontier is in Europe, and Thailand is far ahead in research
vietnam_evidence: Vietnam-affiliated works 2015 to 2026 on extrusion, high-moisture or shear-cell texturisation of meat analogues: 3; Thailand: 31, including high-moisture extrusion of mung bean protein (SLP-06; SLP-07). The 2026 IUH paper (TIC-21) is all-IUH by affiliation but its equipment is unverified (abstract withheld; SLP-07). No Vietnam-affiliated shear-cell or fibre-spinning work. Shear cell is commercial at 'several hundred tons a year' in the Netherlands (SLP-12)
verdict_note: Does not change T1: T1 is dry textured protein by standard extrusion, where cost is set by soy flour, not by texturising technology. Fibre spinning is still research; shear cell is an early commercial European route. Vietnam would buy equipment or licence later. For trials, Thai public extrusion capacity (MTEC, Kasetsart) is nearer than any Vietnamese facility
signal_to_watch: A shear-cell or spinning unit sold or licensed in Asia; a published cost per kg below high-moisture extrusion; confirmation that IUH holds a food extruder (OQ-386)
source_ids: GSD-01; SLP-06; SLP-07; SLP-12; TIC-21; FORM-34

maps_to: TPP-01; TPP-02; TPP-03; TPP-04; TPP-05; TPP-06; DMV-08
vietnam_angle: Already served. The study's target product profiles are open specification sheets (price, protein, format, label, first test) written for Vietnamese buyers
vietnam_evidence: Ten active profiles with price and protein targets and named buyers (ch25 section 25.2); DMV-08 proposes a standing buyer panel to publish specifications and minimum orders
verdict_note: Covered by TPP-01 to TPP-06 and DMV-08. The useful addition is publishing each profile as a one-page sheet when P4 functional data exist
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese buyer or association publishing an ingredient specification

vietnam_angle: Real and already used. Retailer private label is a working chay route
vietnam_evidence: Saigon Co.op has more than 2,500 private-label SKUs from more than 100 Vietnamese makers; all five Co.op Select frozen chay dishes are made by one co-packer, GN Foods; Lotte Mart sells Choice L chay (AIB-28; CPC-15; ECO-35; FORM-01)
verdict_note: Covered by TPP-02 (pitch a 10 g protein version of a Co.op Select product) and the private-label table. No new element
signal_to_watch: A protein claim on a private-label chay product

gfi_title: Plants as a recombinant protein expression platform
vietnam_angle: Weak. Vietnam has crops and genetic-modification research but no buyer, no route and no reason to make these proteins before reference markets do
vietnam_evidence: Molecular farming of animal proteins in soy and pea has US regulatory status reviews (FTB-29; FTB-31) and remains early (FTB-33). In Vietnam a genetically modified crop needs cultivation and food-use certificates (ch07)
verdict_note: Vietnam would buy the ingredient, not make it. Relevant later to T7 buyers (specialty dairy proteins) and to the GMO questions in DMV-16
signal_to_watch: A molecular-farmed food protein approved in Singapore or another ASEAN country, or offered to Vietnamese dairy and nutrition makers

vietnam_angle: None. Turkey is not part of the Vietnamese diet in the study's data, and no buyer asks for it
vietnam_evidence: No turkey appears in the study's diet, retail or buyer data (ch11, app-s2, ch16); the retail audit found no turkey analogue (FORM-01)
verdict_note: No domestic meat to replace and no buyer. Diaspora chay products (TPP-09) follow Vietnamese formats, not turkey

gfi_title: Expanded product development in plant-based meat snacks
vietnam_angle: Already exists in Vietnamese form. Dried chay 'beef, chicken, fish, squid', chay floss and dry soy-gluten 'ribs' are traditional chay formats made from imported soy protein and gluten
vietnam_evidence: A Ho Chi Minh City dealer sells Chinese lines for dried chay snack formats, with no customers named (FORM-34, re-read 2026-10-15); about 40,700 kg of dry soy-and-gluten 'ribs' sold on Lazada (MKT-03); imported mushroom jerky only in premium stores (FORM-01)
verdict_note: The makers of these formats are T1 buyers (TPP-01, TPP-02) and diaspora exporters (TPP-09). No separate snack play: the protein ingredient, not the snack format, is the Vietnamese gap
signal_to_watch: A domestic maker of dried chay snacks naming its textured-protein supplier (OQ-368)

gfi_title: Forging product development partnerships among ingredient suppliers and manufacturers
vietnam_angle: Already happening through distributors; a neutral broker would add little now
vietnam_evidence: ACC and Angel Yeast ran a seminar for Vietnamese food makers in May 2025 and planned 'Innovation Days' at customer sites (AIS-38); distributors such as VMC, TDGIMEX and Brenntag reach small chay makers (ch16)
verdict_note: Covered by DMV-08 (standing buyer panel), the T1 partner list and the TPP-05 first test (samples to two dairy research teams)
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese co-development agreement between a protein maker and a food buyer

gfi_title: Fat and moisture encapsulation for alternative protein products
vietnam_angle: Weak. Vietnamese chay products use palm, soybean or generic vegetable oil; coconut is used only by imported analogues and one small cashew-coconut brand. Fat encapsulation matters for whole cuts, which Vietnam does not make
vietnam_evidence: Retail audit: coconut in two imported Italian frozen analogues, one imported roll, plant milks and one Vietnamese cashew-coconut cheese and yoghurt brand; Vietnamese fillings list palm or soybean oil; frozen analogues median 13 g fat per 100 g (n = 8) (FORM-01). Vietnam crushes about 31 kt of copra and exports little coconut oil (FS-24). Rice bran oil exists (Calofic, FS-29), but no rice-bran-wax oleogel supply was checked
verdict_note: Vietnam would buy fat systems from ingredient houses if it ever made high-moisture whole cuts. Coconut is not a distinctive Vietnamese asset for this use
signal_to_watch: An oleogel or structured plant fat offered by a distributor in Vietnam; a Vietnamese maker starting high-moisture whole cuts

scope_note: Functional protein ingredients for human food
vietnam_angle: Real. Vietnam imports egg white and gelatin for food processing, and the best-known commercial mung bean isolate is an egg substitute, which gives a mung bean isolate a better-priced job than plant milk
vietnam_evidence: Imports in 2025: egg white and egg powders 2,536 t, gelatin 6,778 t (BUY-01; BUY-02); Indian egg white powder USD 5.90 per kg (ch16). FDA had no questions on mung bean protein isolate (more than 80% protein) for uses at 3 to 90% of foods (SLP-11). At mirror bean prices, beans alone cost USD 3.0 to 4.9 per kg of isolate, above Chinese pea protein (USD 2 to 3) but below egg white powder (our calculation; SLP-14; DIE-12)
verdict_note: Adds a second job to T10 and TPP-05: an egg-white replacer (binder and foamer) for processors and bakeries, priced against egg white powder. It competes with the fungal binder in TPP-06. Gelatin replacement is mostly hydrocolloids, not protein, and is outside the study's protein focus
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese processor or bakery trialling a plant egg-white replacer; Chinese mung bean protein offered in Vietnam
source_ids: GSD-01; SLP-11; SLP-14; BUY-01; BUY-02; DIE-12

gfi_title: Hybrid products to optimize nutrition, taste, cost, and sustainability
maps_to: TPP-03; T9; T1; TPP-10; DMV-03; DMV-14
vietnam_angle: Covered in depth. Vietnamese processors already extend with soy; the ceilings are format and sensory, not price
vietnam_evidence: Wave 8 line L6 (HXE) and ch25 set 10 to 20% replacement in fine emulsions and up to 30% in coarse mince; no study supports 50% in pork products; one large processor lists soy in 22 of 67 formulations (HXE-01; HXE-02; BUY-05). GFI's 20 to 50% plant share describes US and European blends and does not transfer
verdict_note: Covered by TPP-03, DMV-03 and DMV-14; cultivated hybrids by TPP-10 and T8
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese processor launching a declared plant-meat blend above 20%

gfi_title: Optimizing fat profiles for nutritional and sensory properties
vietnam_angle: None now. The documented nutrition issue for Vietnamese analogues is sodium, not fat profile, and Vietnam does not make the whole-cut analogues where fat profile is designed
vietnam_evidence: Frozen analogues in the retail audit carry a median 597 mg sodium per 100 g, which fills a child's lunch allowance (NQR-01; FORM-01); 15% of Vietnamese respondents rank lower sodium in their top three reasons to eat more plant-based meat (CON-02)
verdict_note: No Vietnamese buyer or rule asks for fat-profile design. If anything, sodium and protein density come first
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese front-of-pack or claim rule on saturated fat that covers plant-based foods

vietnam_angle: Weak. Vietnamese consumers ask for variety, cooking fit and fewer additives more than a closer copy of meat, and meat flavourings already circulate as imported, repacked products with a fraud reputation
vietnam_evidence: In Vietnam 23% of respondents put 'tasted more like meat' in their top three reasons to eat more plant-based meat, below the six-country average of 28% (CON-02, stated). Beef flavourings at a Ho Chi Minh City market were imported and repacked and used to pass pork off as beef (2011 report, SLP-13). Chay makers get flavour from seasonings (ECO-37; BUY-26)
verdict_note: A catalogue of animal flavour molecules is global research Vietnam would use, not build, and a Vietnamese-dish version has no buyer pull. The live issue is animal-free certification of flavourings for vegan chay claims (DMV-13), not flavour discovery
signal_to_watch: Chay makers seeking certified animal-free meat flavours for TCVN 13625 vegan claims; a published flavour study of a Vietnamese dish base
